plan.description: Infallible allocations in `limbs::rem`/`limbs::mul`; `base_plain`, `rr`, `one_mont`, `product` still plain `Vec`s (`OBL-BN-ALLOCATOR`)
`SecretBuf::from_vec` cleanses initialised length only; spare capacity may retain secret bytes — establish a storage invariant or cleanse the whole allocation
Destructor cleansing is proportional to normalised (secret) length; representation-level fix needed, not a normalisation tweak
Mutate only `cleanse_now()` while keeping the observer, to prove the tests detect uncleansed bytes rather than only the absence of the destructor
EC secret-base reduction: `ecdsa_sign_setup` inverts nonce `k` via `ec_field_inverse_mod_ord`; `ossl_ec_GFp_mont_field_inv` takes field elements; initial `limbs::rem` is variable-time
RSA CRT moduli are secret (only the width is public); Montgomery precomputation runs on them — taint CRT modulus contents, not just exponents
`BN_mod_inverse`: 171 branches + 38 secret-derived addresses + 28 allocator branches; needs a domain-correct constant-time inversion, with a separate variable-time public path
Observable result bit length survives in the returned `BIGNUM` (`store_consttime`)
Secret-length-dependent boundary copy and admission checks (the 19 length-taint sites)
Unify `CleansedScratch<const N>` and `SecretBuf<T>` into one secret-storage policy (`SecretArray<N>`, `SecretBuf<T>`, `SecretLimbs`, `SecretRef`)
RSA blinding lifecycle and CRT recombination review; padding implicit-rejection consistency; error paths not disclosing secret validation state
ECDSA nonce generation, inversion and scalar arithmetic reviewed end to end
`core::hint::black_box` audit — it guarantees nothing; audit every use and every secret-bearing caller of `constant_time.rs`
Optimised-code review: LTO/inlining/cmov-vs-branch, division latency, CPU feature dispatch; automated binary inspection rather than assembly snapshots
Compiler-upgrade policy that invalidates code-generation assurance until rechecked
BINSEC `-checkct` with a validated `-sse-script`; previously exited 0 with no output
Hardware PMU counters
TIMECOP SUPERCOP harness (dormant, pinned to 2018–2019 trees); client-request method available
Fresh binary-bound measurement of the **final** candidate
Byte-reproducible instrumentation build (D255 `.symtab` difference); preserve measured binaries as content-addressed artefacts
Benchmark against reference OpenSSL for RSA/DH/EC workloads
Allocation-failure behaviour for the whole secret-bearing operation, not just ladder scratch
Secret ownership does not propagate through the arithmetic itself

The constant-time inversion's intermediates are ordinary `vec!` allocations at a secret-dependent width (`w.max(a.len())`), so they are infallible, uncleansed on drop, and their geometry may follow secret metadata. Use the same public-width, fallible, auto-cleansed storage as the ladder.
`runtime::secure` init-order instability
Move the `SecretBuf` implementation from `bn::secret` into `runtime::secret` so the runtime-wide abstraction does not depend on the BN subsystem; keep the BN alias and re-run the mutation controls.
Constant-time modular addition and a fixed-width secret store

`BN_div` ignores `BN_FLG_CONSTTIME`: the RSA CRT path has 10 indirect `BN_div` callsites on flagged (secret) operands, and the crate's `div_rem_fallible` branches on a value comparison. Measured at DSO `5d0f9098` with `courts/phase18/timing/binary_branch_audit.py`. Non-smooth and tail error paths, so narrow — but it is a variable-time path on secret operands.

ECDSA signing is allocation-bound: ~75 344 allocations per signature against the reference's 29, and 82.8x the reference wall time. Establish where the per-bit allocations come from in the scalar ladder and the modular arithmetic, then reuse fixed scratch as the exponentiation ladder does. Measure again after.

Secret-bearing vector growth released old blocks before cleansing: `try_assign_limbs` used `Vec::try_reserve_exact` then cleansed only the new block, `bn_wexpand` reserved in place, and `try_boxed` dropped a refused `BIGNUM` normally.

`runtime::obj` tests are not deterministic at the default thread count: a global `NameDb::active_walks` defers a test's removal past its own assertion when a concurrent unlocked `EVP_*_do_all` walk runs. Needs a policy decision (per-test registry instance or a scoped walk lock), not a mechanical lock.
`runtime::mem::tests::array_overflow_returns_null_and_raises` failed once at the default thread count; establish whether it shares the T25 global-state mechanism.
Choose and justify the primary version (9.9p1 backs closures/L7; 10.5p1 backs probe/unit probe); keep the other as a separate cohort
Hermetic environment: pin and verify OpenSSL source, OpenSSH tarball, PuTTY, Dropbear by digest
Install plink/puttygen/dropbear/dbclient/dropbearkey/dropbearconvert **before** configure; verify detection from the generated Makefile and `regress/test-exec.sh` rather than assuming
Build A (reference OpenSSL) and Build B (OpenSSL-RS) from the same unmodified source in isolated trees, no shared `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`
Per-executable runtime identity (`ssh`, `sshd`, `sshd-session`, `ssh-keygen`, `ssh-agent`, `sftp-server`): `readelf -d`, resolved `ldd`, live `/proc/<pid>/maps`; fail closed on mixed linkage
Full upstream `make tests` on both builds; classify every failure as upstream-common / candidate-specific / harness; keep upstream-common failures as failures
Four-cell matrix (A-A, B-B, B-A, A-B) using the upstream harness and `TEST_SSH_SSH`, with isolated ports/config/keys per cell

PuTTY client → OpenSSH server and Dropbear client → OpenSSH server; OpenSSH client → Dropbear server where the harness supports it; record negotiated algorithms from transcripts; distinguish unsupported from failed

Coverage: Ed25519/RSA/ECDSA auth, X25519 and NIST ECDH, FFDH, PQ hybrid, AES-CTR/GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, HMAC integrity failures, host-key rejection, certificates, rekeying, agent, concurrent sessions

Harness negative controls: wrong client binary, wrong crypto library, failed auth, dead server, unsupported algorithm, missing third-party tool, timeout/signal kill; harness must fail if a control does not trigger
Machine-readable manifests, exact executed/skipped/blocked counts, reproduction commands; no hand-authored totals
Reconcile the historical 9.9p1/10.5p1 populations in one receipt so their results are never treated as interchangeable

Evidence and trust audit: inventory formats, receipts, identities, adjudications, release tooling; find every truncation, silent suppression, summary-without-reconstruction and wrong-candidate application
SARIF 2.1.0 (+ Errata 01) interoperability profile; deterministic adapter for representative real findings (BN timing, unsafe-boundary obligations, curl element-7 refusals, OpenSSH adjudication)

Lossless evidence preservation: original output, args, instrument identity, candidate identity, population, counts, unsupported ops, timeouts; content-addressed; reconciliation of native vs exported populations
Identity model: rule identity / logical finding identity / exact occurrence identity; fingerprints never authorise reuse across artefacts; conservative on collisions and code movement
Rust/FFI/binary location fidelity: macro expansion, monomorphisation, C ABI, indirect dispatch, optimised code; no fabricated line precision for machine-code findings

Completeness and execution admission: expected vs examined population, unsupported constructs, skips, timeouts, truncation; an absent population is not an empty population; exit code is not completeness
Suppression governance: a suppressed finding remains a finding; justification, scope, evidence, reviewer, independence, expiry, consequences; auto-invalidate on change
Baselines and honest regression tracking: distinguish root-cause elimination and proved unreachable from tool-stopped-reporting; no artificial monotonicity
GitHub code-scanning integration without GitHub dependency: full local artefacts authoritative; shard manifest when export limits truncate (5 000-result limit)
in-toto Statement v1 typed attestations; SLSA provenance predicate only for genuine SLSA statements; versioned project predicate types for everything else
DSSE authentication with the exact PAE over the received bytes; never reparse/reserialise before verification; `keyid` is an unauthenticated hint only
DSSE parser hardening: duplicate JSON keys, invalid encodings, oversized payloads, signature-count bounds, algorithm downgrade refusal, forward-extension discipline
Independent cryptographic verification of envelopes: the root of trust must not be the unverified candidate; keep verification deps out of `libcrypto`/`libssl`
Signature reproducibility vs artefact reproducibility kept separate; never seed production randomness for reproducible signatures

Role-bound authorisation: maintainer, source/build/analysis/proof producer, instrument reviewer, adjudicator, external reproducer, release authority, revocation authority; wrong-role signature insufficient
Thresholds over distinct authorised keys and distinct trust domains; repeated signatures and aliases cannot satisfy independence
Sigstore bundle profile with certificates, transparency entries, inclusion proofs, timestamps; offline verification with stated trust-root/freshness assumptions
Transparency and omission resistance: freeze an expected evidence manifest before execution; close with a signed reconciliation manifest; a producer cannot PASS by omitting a failed result
Survivable key compromise (TUF principles): rotation, delegation, expiry, revocation, anti-rollback, anti-freeze; old signatures never authorise a stale release
Authenticated corrections and retractions: append-only, bound to the original attestation, propagating invalidation; preserve what was believed and what was disproved
Deterministic policy engine: conjunction of obligations, not a score; denial-by-default; a candidate may not choose a permissive policy for itself
Verification-summary attestations after policy evaluation; a summary never replaces the evidence for independent reconstruction

Adversarial qualification: the eight mandatory experiments (stripped results, wrong-binary proof, self-signed independence, crashed-but-empty report, one-person-two-credentials, withdrawn claim, reproducible-but-defective binary, complete-and-independent evidence)

Formal verification of the verifier: the smallest evidence-processing core; verify that required evidence cannot be omitted, signatures cannot imply semantic correctness, substitution cannot preserve acceptance

External verification package: frozen manifest, provenance, full SARIF, native evidence, reconciliation, envelopes, statements, bundles, policy, controls, rebuild instructions; treat remote evidence as hostile
Extended public verifier surface (`verify sarif
Verification economics: FAST/BATCH/BOUNDARY/SEAL/EXTERNAL; sign immutable manifests rather than every report; never trade completeness for cost

Vertical slice first: real frozen finding → native evidence → SARIF → content-addressed manifest → in-toto statement → DSSE → independent verification → policy adjudication → reproducible result; then the deliberately corrupted counterpart

Protocol and infrastructure audit: inspect the current ETP, SARIF, DSSE and release infrastructure; pin admitted Rekor, Sigstore, timestamping and C2SP versions; identify actual client support, signing configuration, witness availability and trust assumptions. Evidence: a tracked registry naming each admitted version, digest and unsupported feature, plus the recorded service-configuration finding

Local vertical slice: pinned POSIX-backed Rekor v2 instance; publish one real frozen ETP statement through the supported `hashedrekord` path; verify binding, inclusion and checkpoint; archive the complete evidence; execute the relevant corruption controls (§B.24 items 1–12, 14–16, 18–20)
Trusted timestamping and offline verification: RFC 3161 timestamp evidence integrated; verification demonstrated without the original live service; the nine separate times of §B.9 recorded distinctly
Campaign accountability: opening, amendment, closure and abandonment records; omission-sensitive reconciliation that refuses a closure omitting an applicable failure (§B.13–B.14)
Public transparency: admitted public-good Rekor v2 profile; only classified release-critical material published; independently executable verification demonstrated

Consistency, monitoring and witnesses: persistent checkpoint state, consistency verification and monitoring; genuinely independent witnesses admitted when available; split-view controls demonstrated (§B.7, §B.11–B.12)

Archival and revocation: durable evidence reconstruction, current-state metadata, authenticated correction and anti-rollback controls; a withdrawn claim refused by current-state policy while its original inclusion proof stays valid (§B.17, §B.19)
Formal assurance: transparency-policy invariants of §B.23 verified in a small model; tool assumptions and the refinement gap recorded
Continuous enforcement: admitted profile integrated into `AGENTS.md`, release gates, ETP claim schemas, CI and public non-claims; silent regression prevented

Close or honestly hold the 27 named element-7 refusals (`http` 4 local-copy sites; `provider/rand`, `confmod`, `evp_pbe`, `encoder_meth`, `rand_lib`, PEM pair, `passphrase`, `store_result`, `obj`, `stack`, `ui_read`, `check_crl`, `dh/check`)
Reconcile the running site count against the named rows (the ±1/±2 discrepancies recorded in the batch notes)
One frozen census → freeze → closure run at a single identity after the tool changes
Independent adversarial review of the ~9,600 new lines in `consumer_closure.py` (CFG dominance, frame-slot scans, DSO-local copies, callback writers)
Curl L7 replay at the final candidate; element-7 PASS; graduation record; counter 2/33 only if the safety argument survives independent review
